name: serpentinizing_vent_reactor_reduced
description: Reduced tuned-relaxation vent reactor (fallback / A-B comparison): Gaussian serpentinization source feeding a first-order relaxation box. Runs anywhere (no phreeqpython/fipy). NOT real geochemistry.

flow_velocity.description: Boundary water flux through the reaction zone (m/s)

t_target.description: Mixing-target temperature (K); Lost City mid-window ~340 K

h2_rate_max.description: Peak H2 source rate at reference flow (mol/s)

serpentinization.doc:
Reduced serpentinization source: ``(T, flow) -> H2 / alkalinity / heat``.

REDUCED REPRODUCTION, not PHREEQC/Reaktoro. Each tick it (a) adds the
integrated H2 + alkalinity + heat it produced over the interval to the vent
stores (bare ``float`` deltas, so they accumulate and compose), and (b)
publishes the instantaneous source *rates* as ``overwrite[float]`` sensor
readings for observability. Production peaks in a temperature window and
scales with water flux (serpentinization is water–rock-reaction limited).

_contract.summary: Reduced serpentinization source (clean-room stand-in, NOT PHREEQC): (T, flow) -> H2, alkalinity, heat source rates.
_contract.description: Deliberately reduced parameterized reproduction of the serpentinizing source for Campaign 0 - the real model is PhreeqcSerpentinizationProcess. Each tick it adds the integrated H2 + alkalinity + heat produced over the interval to the vent stores (additive float deltas) and publishes the instantaneous source rates as overwrite sensors. Production peaks in a Gaussian temperature window and saturates with water flux (serpentinization is water-rock-reaction limited) - right order of magnitude and sign, so the vent composite runs end to end and settles into a Lost City-like window.
math: activity(T, flow) = exp(-(T - t_opt)^2 / (2 t_width^2)) * flow / (flow + flow_ref)
rate_i = rate_max_i * activity;   pool_i += rate_i * dt
assumptions: Reduced reproduction, not a geochemical solver: a smooth parameterized source, right magnitude/sign only.
activity = Gaussian temperature window * saturating flow dependence; rate = rate_max * activity.

reactor.doc:
Reduced vent–ocean mixing reactor.

Read–modify–write: reads the current ``temperature``/``pH``/``porosity`` plus
the serpentinization drivers, and emits first-order relaxation **deltas**
toward field-constrained targets (bare ``float`` ports, so the deltas compose
additively and a sibling process could also contribute).

_contract.summary: Reduced vent-ocean mixing reactor (clean-room stand-in, NOT FiPy): relaxes T / pH / porosity toward Lost City-like field targets.
_contract.description: Deliberately reduced well-mixed reactor reproduction for Campaign 0 - the real model is FipyReactiveTransportProcess. Read-modify-write: reads the current temperature / pH / porosity and the serpentinization drivers and emits first-order relaxation deltas toward field-constrained targets (additive float ports), so a short run settles into the Lost City window (~45-90 C, pH ~9-10.8) with a sustained reducing supply. Temperature is nudged by accumulated serpentinization heat; pH tracks an alkalinity-driven target; porosity evolves toward a precipitation-set value (clamped to [0, 1]).
math: dpH = k_ph * (ph_base + (ph_max - ph_base) * alk/(alk + alk_scale) - pH) * dt
d(porosity) = k_porosity * (porosity_target - porosity) * dt,  clamped to [0, 1]
assumptions: Reduced reproduction, not a reactive-transport solver: well-mixed first-order relaxation to field targets.
Targets field-constrained to the Lost City window; porosity clamped to [0, 1].

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
